questions.text: What are the four classical components that cause variations in a time series data analysis?
questions.answer: Trend, Seasonal, Cyclical, Irregular (Random)
questions.explanation: These four elements explain the movements or variations of data points over a specific time period.

questions.text: What is the primary statistical purpose of constructing a linear regression model in business analytics?
questions.answer: To estimate/predict the value of a dependent variable
questions.explanation: Regression draws a line of best fit to predict outcomes based on independent variables.

questions.text: State the fundamental formula used to calculate a simple price index number relative to a predetermined base year.
questions.answer: (Current Year Value / Base Year Value) * 100
questions.explanation: Used to measure relative changes in prices, quantities, or values over time.

questions.text: Specify the exact mathematical range within which the Pearson product-moment correlation coefficient must always fall.
questions.answer: Between -1 and +1
questions.explanation: A value of +1 signifies a perfect positive relationship, -1 indicates perfect negative, and 0 means no linear relationship.

questions.text: Identify the two foundational rules of probability that apply to mutually exclusive events and independent events, respectively.
questions.answer: Addition rule (OR) and Multiplication rule (AND)
questions.explanation: Used for mutually exclusive events and independent events, respectively.

questions.text: What are the three most common statistical measures utilized to determine the central tendency of a given dataset?
questions.answer: Mean, Median, Mode
questions.explanation: These are the three most common ways to find the center or typical value of a dataset.

questions.text: Describe the mathematical procedure, or formula, used to calculate the variance of a population data set.
questions.answer: Sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by N
questions.explanation: Variance measures how far a set of numbers is spread out from their average value.

questions.text: Outline the sequential steps a statistician must follow when conducting a formal hypothesis test.
questions.answer: State hypothesis, select significance level, compute test statistic, make decision
questions.explanation: These four fundamental steps are used to evaluate claims about a population parameter.

questions.text: In what specific analytical scenarios is the Chi-square non-parametric test most appropriately applied?
questions.answer: Testing goodness of fit and independence of variables
questions.explanation: It compares observed frequencies against expected frequencies for categorical data.

questions.text: Name three widely used quantitative forecasting techniques applied in the analysis of historical business data.
questions.answer: Moving Average, Exponential Smoothing, Trend Projection
questions.explanation: These are common quantitative models used to predict future values from past historical data.

questions.text: List the primary probability and non-probability sampling techniques utilized in statistical data collection.
questions.answer: Random, Stratified, Systematic, Cluster, Quota
questions.explanation: Methods used to select a subset of individuals from a population to estimate characteristics of the whole.

questions.text: What is the ultimate mathematical objective of formulating a linear programming problem in operations research?
questions.answer: To maximize profit or minimize cost subject to constraints
questions.explanation: LP uses linear mathematical models to achieve the best outcome derived from scarce resources.

questions.text: State the formula utilized in Cost-Volume-Profit analysis to calculate the break-even point in units.
questions.answer: Fixed Costs / Contribution Margin per Unit
questions.explanation: Shows the exact number of units that must be sold to cover all fixed and variable costs.

questions.text: How is the traditional payback period calculated for a prospective capital investment project?
questions.answer: Initial Investment / Annual Cash Inflow
questions.explanation: It assesses the time required to recoup the funds expended in an investment (ignoring time value of money).

questions.text: State the definitive decision rule governing whether an investment project should be accepted or rejected based on its Net Present Value (NPV).
questions.answer: Accept the project if Net Present Value is positive
questions.explanation: A positive NPV indicates that the projected earnings (discounted for time value of money) exceed the anticipated costs.

questions.text: Provide a practical interpretation of what the standard deviation represents in relation to a dataset's mean.
questions.answer: The average distance of data points from the mean
questions.explanation: It expresses data volatility and reliability; a high SD indicates high variance.

questions.text: Explain the primary analytical purpose of calculating moving averages when analyzing a sequence of time-series data.
questions.answer: Smooths out short-term fluctuations to highlight longer-term trends
questions.explanation: Moving averages filter out the 'noise' from random price or data fluctuations.

questions.text: What does a Z-score precisely measure when standardizing data within a normal probability distribution?
questions.answer: Measures number of standard deviations from the mean
questions.explanation: It helps standardize values on different scales so they can be compared using the standard normal probability table.

questions.text: Define the concept of a decision tree analysis and its application in evaluating competing business alternatives under uncertainty.
questions.answer: Visual model mapping sequential decisions and outcomes
questions.explanation: Decision trees calculate expected values of competing alternatives using probabilities.

questions.text: What specific types of mathematical skills and concepts are predominantly tested in the objective section of the Quantitative Analysis examination?
questions.answer: Tests fundamental concepts and basic calculations
questions.explanation: The objective section is designed to test wide syllabus coverage rather than deep, multi-step problem solving.
